subject: Clearline launch: throttle thresholds & production metrics request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Clearline launch: throttle thresholds & production metrics request

Team —

Quick context: Clearline (CL-4821) confirmed a product launch window the week of Nov 23. Their preflight traffic model (attached) shows a short burst pattern during day-1 onboarding and sustained higher baseline by day-3. Sales needs a temporary uplift to their per-tenant rate ceilings and clarification on the telemetry we can provide during the ramp.

Asks:
- Can we temporarily raise their per-tenant throttle ceilings from current 500 RPS to 1,500 RPS (US region) for a 72-hour window around their launch?
- If 1,500 RPS is not safe, provide the maximum safe burst we can guarantee and whether we can gate by time windows.
- We also need per-route production metrics (p90 latency by endpoint, token-level error rates, KV cache hit-rate) surfaced to Clearline during the ramp and retained for 30 days.

Dependencies: product confirmation for fallback model variants and cache warmup, infra confirmation for capacity and routing, and CS / legal sign-off for a short SLA carve-out.

I've attached the Clearline traffic model they just sent. Can we get feasibility + a proposed implementation plan by EOD Friday (11/13)?

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clearline launch: throttle thresholds & production metrics request

Thanks Karthik —

A few clarifying questions before David sizes the request:
1) Are the 1,500 RPS bursts global (all regions) or strictly US? You noted US above but confirm.
2) Does Clearline expect sustained 1,500 RPS after the 72-hour window or is that purely an onboarding spike? The attached sheet looks like an onboarding spike + then a higher baseline (~600–700 RPS).
3) For the telemetry ask: do they need raw token traces, or aggregated metrics (p50/p90/p99 latency, error rate, cache hit-rate) exposed via the Console and pushed to a shared dashboard? Aggregates are much cheaper to retain.

Product asks / concerns for Marissa:
- Can we guarantee model-variant fallback (smaller quantized model) on overload, and what does that mean for latency/cost expectations?
- Can we pre-warm / pre-populate KV caches for keys they expect to hit during onboarding (documented model inputs)?

David — once we confirm the above, can you provide: safe burst ceiling, config changes needed (routing keys / feature flags), rollback plan, and estimated ops time to implement? If we need reserved capacity mapping, call that out.

Karthik — loop in Clearline to confirm exact timestamps they want the window.

—Mina
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clearline launch: throttle thresholds & production metrics request

Mina / team —

Short answer: technically feasible, with caveats.

What we can do:
- Temporary per-tenant burst uplift: we can increase the soft throttle ceiling from 500 -> 1,500 RPS in the US region for a defined window, provided we carve out capacity on a reserved pool or map Clearline to a dedicated slice for that window. Without reserved capacity, the uplift is best-effort and could impact other tenants.
- Canary & rollback: we should schedule a 30-minute canary at launch start (1% traffic or limited IP subset) and a 2-hour observation window before allowing full ramp. Automated rollback triggers should include sustained tail-latency > 2x baseline or error rate > 3%.
- Telemetry: we can deliver aggregated metrics (p50/p90/p99 latency, token-error-rate, KV hit-rate) via a shared Console dashboard and export to their Grafana (we already support Prometheus -> remote_write). Raw token traces are not feasible without a legal / privacy exception.

Work required:
1) Routing config: a temporary feature-flagged routing policy + dedicated pool mapping (we will need an infra runbook).
2) Capacity reservation: open a reserved-capacity ticket; estimate: 1 days scheduling + 2 days provisioning if using shared infra pools. If they want dedicated hardware, lead time is ~2 weeks.
3) Instrumentation: product to confirm telemetry endpoints; infra to wire up dashboard and retention policy (30 days).

I'll attach a stub (capacity_change_req.yaml) with the settings I propose.

Risks: collateral impact on multi-tenant latency; billing/entitlements must be clear before we enable (sales/legal).

Planned ETA: If we approve a reserved pool (short-term carve-out), I can enact the routing and flag changes by Nov 20 EOD.

-David
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Mina / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming: the 1,500 RPS burst is US-only and is expected to be a Day-0 onboarding spike (approx 6 hours), after which traffic drops to ~600–700 RPS baseline by Day 3. We do not expect sustained 1,500 RPS beyond the onboarding window.

We prefer aggregated metrics exposed to the Console and a push to our Grafana. Raw token traces not necessary.

Attached: clearline_traffic_model.xlsx (sheet "Launch_Ramp_v2"). Proposed launch window: Nov 24 03:00–09:00 PST for onboarding spike; open to shifting by a day if that helps your canary schedule.

Let me know what you need from our side (expected IP ranges, test tokens for canary subset).

Best,
Alice
Head of Integrations, Clearline

Quick sync summary / action items (Clearline / CL-4821) —

Action items & owners:
- David Kim: implement temporary routing + feature flag for burst uplift; prepare capacity_change_req.yaml and reserve pool carve-out if needed. ETA: Nov 20 EOD. If dedicated hardware required, escalate immediately. (Owner: david_kim@redwood.com)
- Marissa Cole: confirm model-variant fallback behavior and KV pre-warm plan; update product runbook with acceptable latency bands for the fallback model. ETA: Nov 18 EOD. (Owner: marissa_cole@redwood.com)
- Karthik Iyer: finalize SLA carve-out, entitlements language with Legal/CS, and lock the exact onboarding timestamps with Clearline (confirm by Nov 16). (Owner: karthik_iyer@redwood.com)
- Mina Haddad (me): coordinate canary plan (30-min 1% traffic) and rollback triggers; own post-launch review. ETA: Nov 23 morning.

Telemetry: David — please confirm the Console dashboard link and the Grafana remote_write config by Nov 19. Attachments referenced: clearline_traffic_model.xlsx (from Clearline), prod-metrics-specs.pdf (our instrumentation spec), capacity_change_req.yaml (infra stub).

If anyone sees any blocker to the dates above, flag immediately. I'll run a 15-minute cross-functional call Monday (11/16) to finalize the runbook if needed.

Thanks —
Mina
